pr.title: match lowering: consistently merge simple or-patterns
pr.description:
There are two places where we expand or-patterns in match lowering: the main one is `test_candidates_with_or`, and there's one in `match_candidates` that's an optimization for the simple case where the whole pattern is just one or-pattern.

To reduce duplication, we merge or-pattern alternatives into a single block when possible, but we only to that in `test_candidates_with_or`. This PR fixes this oversight and merges them in `match_candidates` too.

This is a part of splitting up https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/122046 into smaller bits.
pr.author: Nadrieril

processing.reason: The PR's historical transformation is a semantics-preserving MIR CFG cleanup, not a value-changing rewrite. In the pre-PR match_candidates fast path, a whole-pattern or-pattern was split into trivial subcandidates whose separate pre-binding blocks each jumped to the same binding/result block; the corrected code additionally calls merge_trivial_subcandidates, redirecting both alternatives to one shared any_matches block (as shown by issue_75439's `0` and `4294901760` both targeting bb3). All value assignments, bindings, guards, and the result remain identical. Guards and non-trivial subcandidates are explicitly excluded from merging, so there is no input on which the original and corrected lowering produce different defined numeric/boolean/character results. Any function pair that differed would have to invent an unrelated semantic change, which the task forbids; the only observable difference is duplicated CFG blocks versus merged blocks.

analysis.summary: Match lowering has two or-pattern expansion sites, but only test_candidates_with_or merged trivial subcandidates; the match_candidates fast path for a whole-pattern or-pattern did not. The PR records the or-pattern span on Candidate and invokes merge_trivial_subcandidates after processing split candidates, removing duplicate alternative blocks and reducing CFG size. This is an optimization/CFG-cleanup PR, evidenced by the updated MatchBranchSimplification mir-opt expectation.
analysis.originalLogic: Or-patterns are expanded in two places: test_candidates_with_or and the match_candidates optimization for when the whole pattern is a single or-pattern. Only test_candidates_with_or called merge_trivial_subcandidates, which merges alternatives into one join block when possible; the match_candidates path created subcandidates but left each alternative with its own pre-binding block and duplicated code/gotos.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect behavior was inconsistent simplification: after match_candidates replaced an or-pattern with subcandidates, it did not call merge_trivial_subcandidates. The resulting MIR kept separate alternative blocks (e.g. bb4 and bb5 each loading `_4 = _2[3 of 4]` and jumping to bb3) instead of routing all trivial alternatives to a shared any_matches block. The corrected transformation calls merge_trivial_subcandidates for every split candidate, preserving the or-pattern span on the Candidate so the shared-block gotos carry the right source info.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR match lowering for a match whose whole pattern is a simple or-pattern with no guard, where all alternatives are trivial (no remaining subcandidates or match pairs) so their pre-binding blocks can be merged. The updated regression is issue_75439's `foo` on a transmuted `[u32; 4]`, with an or-pattern on element 2 whose alternatives both lead to the same binding/result block.
analysis.trigger: candidates are split into subcandidates in match_candidates (split_or_candidate is set), then match_simplified_candidates is called; afterwards each original candidate has non-empty subcandidates, no guard, and every subcandidate is trivial enough to merge.
preconditions: The whole pattern is a simple or-pattern handled by the match_candidates fast path.
candidate.subcandidates is non-empty and candidate.has_guard is false.
Every subcandidate has empty subcandidates and empty match_pairs, so can_merge remains true.
The or-pattern span is recorded whenever subcandidates are created: invariant 'it is `None` iff `subcandidates.is_empty()`'.
pitfalls: Do not merge when the candidate has a guard: the code returns early on `candidate.subcandidates.is_empty() || candidate.has_guard`.
Do not merge unless all subcandidates are trivial; recursion must compute can_merge without short-circuiting: 'Not `Iterator::all` because we don't want to short-circuit.'
Set or_span at every site that assigns subcandidates; otherwise the merge's `candidate.or_span.take().unwrap()` can fail or attach the wrong span.
The changed test is named MatchBranchSimplification, but the patch modifies match lowering; do not misattribute the CFG change itself to the MatchBranchSimplification pass.
This is an optimization/oversight fix, not a demonstrated miscompilation; the description says match_candidates is 'an optimization for the simple case'.
analysis.testStrategy: Add or extend a mir-opt test such as tests/mir-opt/issues/issue_75439.foo.MatchBranchSimplification.diff with a match over a whole or-pattern whose alternatives are trivial. Compare MIR before/after: the corrected output should have the switchInt alternatives target one shared block (e.g. both `0` and `4294901760` going to bb3) and should not emit separate blocks that each duplicate the same StorageLive/load and jump. Also verify a guarded or-pattern and a non-trivial alternative are not merged. Inspect the recorded or_span on each subcandidate-creating path; no compiler was built, so treat this as an inspection-based test strategy rather than an execution claim.
evidence: There are two places where we expand or-patterns in match lowering: the main one is `test_candidates_with_or`, and there's one in `match_candidates` that's an optimization for the simple case where the whole pattern is just one or-pattern.

To reduce duplication, we merge or-pattern alternatives into a single block when possible, but we only to that in `test_candidates_with_or`. This PR fixes this oversight and merges them in `match_candidates` too.
We have to make sure we set it everywhere that we set `subcandidates`.
This avoids exponentially large CFGs in cases like `(1 | 2, 3 | 4, ...)`.
Not `Iterator::all` because we don't want to short-circuit.
-          switchInt(_2[2 of 4]) -> [0: bb4, 4294901760: bb5, otherwise: bb6];
+          switchInt(_2[2 of 4]) -> [0: bb3, 4294901760: bb3, otherwise: bb4];
